thornthwaite.citation: Thornthwaite, C.W. (1948) An Approach toward a Rational Classification of Climate. Geographical Review, 38, 55-94. https://doi.org/10.2307/210739
thornthwaite.worked_example_source: Watson, I. and Burnett, A.D. (1995) Hydrology: An Environmental Approach. Lewis Publishers/CRC Press, ISBN 978-1-56670-087-0. Worked Example 19-2 (Thornthwaite potential evapotranspiration).
thornthwaite.why_secondary_source: The 1948 Geographical Review article is not freely accessible (JSTOR paywall, pre-1996 U.S. copyright); Watson & Burnett's textbook reproduces Thornthwaite's own worked calculation with full inputs and outputs and is the same source already used to validate PyETo (github.com/woodcrafty/PyETo, tests/test_thornthwaite.py), the upstream project climate_indices.eto credits in its module docstring.

inputs.monthly_temps_celsius: thornthwaite_monthly_temps_celsius.npy — mean monthly air temperature, Jan-Dec, as printed in the worked example
inputs.monthly_mean_daylight_hours: thornthwaite_monthly_mean_daylight_hours.npy — mean daylight hours per month as printed in the worked example; not used directly by climate_indices.eto.eto_thornthwaite (which derives daylight hours from latitude), included here for traceability to the source

expected_output.expected_pet_mm: thornthwaite_expected_pet_mm.npy — potential evapotranspiration (mm/month) as printed in the worked example

thornthwaite.latitude_derivation: Not stated by the secondary source (which supplies monthly_mean_daylight_hours directly rather than a latitude). Back-solved by climate_indices as the Northern-Hemisphere latitude whose climate_indices.eto._monthly_mean_daylight_hours(latitude, leap=False) output most closely matches the source's monthly_mean_daylight_hours array (max deviation 0.36 hours, at latitude=43.08 degrees N; 43.0 degrees N was used for simplicity with negligible difference in output).
thornthwaite.data_start_year_rationale: Arbitrary non-leap year; the source does not tie the example to a specific calendar year.
thornthwaite.tolerance_rationale: atol=4.0 mm matches the tolerance PyETo's own test suite established for this exact source (test_thornthwaite in tests/test_thornthwaite.py: 'small difference in estimated monthly PET of up to +/- 4 mm' from the source's rounded coefficients, rounded intermediate values, and no day-count adjustment). climate_indices.eto.eto_thornthwaite run at latitude=43.0, data_start_year=2001 reproduces the source's 12 monthly PET values with a maximum absolute difference of 2.77 mm, within that tolerance.

hargreaves.citation: Hargreaves, G.H. and Samani, Z.A. (1985) Reference Crop Evapotranspiration from Temperature. Applied Engineering in Agriculture, 1(2), 96-99.
hargreaves.worked_example_source: Mehta, V.K. (2006) Estimating Evapotranspiration from Weather Data. Arghyam / Cornell University, as reproduced in PyETo (github.com/woodcrafty/PyETo, tests/test_fao.py::test_hargreaves), the upstream project climate_indices.eto credits in its module docstring.
hargreaves.why_secondary_source: The original 1985 Applied Engineering in Agriculture article is paywalled and not reachable from this environment; the worked example is a faithful application of Equation 52 in Allen et al. (1998) FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (the same equation climate_indices.eto.eto_hargreaves implements, per its own docstring), and is the exact fixture PyETo itself uses to validate its Hargreaves implementation.

inputs.tmin_tmax_tmean_celsius: hargreaves_daily_tmin_tmax_tmean_celsius.npy — [tmin, tmax, tmean] in degrees Celsius, as printed in the worked example

expected_output.expected_eto_mm_per_day: hargreaves_expected_eto_mm_per_day.npy — reference evapotranspiration in mm/day, quoted to 1 decimal place in the worked example

hargreaves.derivation: The worked example supplies extraterrestrial radiation (et_rad = 38.93715 MJ/m2/day) directly rather than a latitude and day of year, because PyETo's hargreaves() function takes et_rad as an input. climate_indices.eto.eto_hargreaves instead derives et_rad internally from latitude and day of year, so climate_indices back-solved the (latitude, day_of_year) pair reproducing that et_rad value via climate_indices.eto's own solar geometry functions: latitude=-12.3 degrees, day_of_year=58 reproduces et_rad=38.937149 MJ/m2/day (difference 1.3e-6), which is exact to the precision the source value is quoted at.
hargreaves.tolerance_rationale: atol=0.05 mm/day reflects the source's 1-decimal-place precision (6.1 mm/day). climate_indices.eto.eto_hargreaves(tmin=28, tmax=38, tmean=35, latitude_degrees=-12.3) evaluated at day_of_year=58 (index 57 of a 366-day year) returns 6.1008 mm/day, a difference of 0.0008 mm/day from the source value.
